_readme: Fill the Hole levels, in play order. Build with: python3 docs/game/build_game.py
map: a file in docs/game/maps/. kicker: the island (see islands). tools: locks, pi.
pick: either {"start": colouring} or constraints on the start state: dF (int or [lo, hi]), dl, locks, N, onLoop,
exits (quietOnly | loudOnly | piOnly), deepest, piRule (loops | par | over); prefer: sort keys such as
"-difficulty", "+difficulty", "+N", "-N", "+dF", "-dF", "+shortWin", "+fewWins". Ties go to the smallest state key.
expect: facts the build asserts (par, onLoop, loopLength, loops, N, unique, deepest, piRunN).
legacy: level ids in the order of the old 20-level game (old saves were keyed by position).
New maps and levels from other sessions: send a level request (LEVEL-REQUEST.md, tools/level_request.py).

levels.title: Splash!
levels.intro: Welcome! The grey ? tile in the middle wants an element, but its ring holds fire AND water. Drag from tile to tile along a little group of fire and water until every tile glows, then press SWAP. Make the ring all one element!

levels.title: One of each
levels.intro: Now there are three elements, and the ring round the ? has one of each. Catch any chain that touches the ring and swap it: the ring keeps only two elements, and the ? can take the third.

levels.title: Forked path
levels.intro: Fire is on the ring twice, water and air only once: swap water or air away. Some chains fork. Trace every arm until the whole chain glows, then swap it.

levels.title: First lock
levels.intro: A chain that joins ring tiles of both its elements is a lock (🔒): swapping it just shuffles the ring. Skip the big locks and find a small chain that clears an element.

levels.title: Spark
levels.intro: The silver platform in the middle has no element yet, because its five rim tiles hold all four. Drag across two neighbouring tiles of different elements to trace their chain, then tap it to swap the two elements. Leave the rim with only three.

levels.title: Ripples
levels.intro: The silver platform in the middle has no element yet, because its five rim tiles hold all four. A few more tiles. Look for the rim element that appears only once, and swap it away.

levels.title: Archipelago
levels.intro: The silver platform in the middle has no element yet, because its five rim tiles hold all four. Bigger island, same trick: one swap clears an element off the rim. Trace the whole chain before you flip it.

levels.title: Big water
levels.intro: The silver platform in the middle has no element yet, because its five rim tiles hold all four. The biggest island in the game, but still one swap. Chains can run far across the island; follow the bridges.

levels.title: First flip
levels.intro: The real tutorial. Trace a chain: drag (or tap tile by tile) across neighbours that alternate two elements, until every tile of that chain glows. Then tap the chain to swap its two elements. Clear one element off the rim.

levels.title: Open doors
levels.intro: A bigger island, still no locks. Chains near the rim score triple and double. You need a chain that changes one rim tile without dragging another rim tile along.

levels.title: One lock
levels.intro: A chain that joins two rim tiles is a lock (🔒): flipping it just moves the problem round the rim. One of Kempe's two classic swaps is locked here. Find the open one.

levels.title: Kempe's double
levels.intro: Both locks are shut: this is the case Kempe faced in 1879. His fix: two swaps on chains of the repeated element, one from each copy of it. Here that works. Par is 2.

levels.title: Heawood's catch
levels.intro: Doubly locked again, but now Kempe's double swap fails in both orders: the first swap reconnects the chain the second one needed. This is the gap Heawood found in 1890. Two swaps still do it; find another pair.

levels.title: Far away
levels.intro: Every quickest solution starts with a chain that never touches the rim. Look away from the platform: change the island far out so that a rim swap opens up.

levels.title: Round and round
levels.intro: A small island with a loop in it. The rim is doubly locked, so the wheel marks one chain π. Flip π, then the new π, and so on: after 20 flips you are back here and the rim never opened. Some other chain leads off the loop. Par is 3.

levels.title: The loop
levels.intro: At a doubly locked rim one canonical chain is left, marked π on the wheel. Flip π, trace the new π, flip again: after 20 flips you are back where you started and the rim never opens. Every one of the 98 such loops in the order-34 census can be left by some other chain. Find it.

levels.title: Quiet way out
levels.intro: You are on a π loop again. This time every quickest way off it starts with a quiet chain: one that touches no rim tile at all. Look away from the platform first.

levels.title: Loud way out
levels.intro: Another loop, and the opposite lesson: no quiet chain helps here. The way off is a chain that touches the rim but is not π. Which rim chain breaks the rhythm?

levels.title: Rigid
levels.intro: The chain counter reads 8, the fewest possible: every chain on the island touches the rim. Only two different swaps change anything here, π and the swap that undoes the last π, and both keep the rim locked. Pick the direction that leads off the loop.

levels.title: Twin loops
levels.intro: This hole has two separate π loops, 20 flips each. You start on one of them. Get off without sliding onto the other.

The longest run of its kind in the 2.8 billion graphs of order 34: following π keeps the rim locked for 8 flips while the total chain count N goes 9, 8, 9, 8, … (watch the chain counter). Proving such a run can never close into a loop is an open problem (NRC). You don't have to follow π.

expect.record: longest DL pi-run with N <= 9 at this hole

levels.title: The cage
levels.intro: A football-shaped island: the map of the C60 molecule. Every rim tile here has six neighbours (a 66666 ring), the ring type with the most room to hide. Two swaps.

levels.title: The six-ring trap
levels.intro: The 66666 hole from "The Six-Ring Trap" page. Of its 1,118 colourings this is the only one four swaps from a fillable rim.

levels.title: Depth 3
levels.intro: Same map. This state needs 3 swaps. Plan ahead: the swaps that look good next to the rim are traps.

levels.title: The tidy trap
levels.intro: Only 17 regions, but just a quarter of their colourings leave the rim fillable, and this one needs four swaps. Small is not easy.

levels.title: Depth 4
levels.intro: Same map. This state needs 4 swaps. Plan ahead: the swaps that look good next to the rim are traps.

levels.title: Depth 5
levels.intro: Same map. This state needs 5 swaps. Plan ahead: the swaps that look good next to the rim are traps.

levels.title: The second pit
levels.intro: A 56666 hole from the order-34 census. One colouring sits five swaps from a fillable rim. This is it.

levels.title: The deepest pit
levels.intro: Of all 7,481 colourings at this record hole, this is the one farthest from a fillable rim: 6 swaps. Nobody has a proof that the distance stays bounded on bigger maps. Can you find the way out?
